title: Governed async replan provider — durable candidate staging bridges the async Planner Pool to the synchronous RuntimePlanner REPLAN path (isolated feature flag, default OFF)
description: Production REPLAN has failed closed FAIL_CLOSED_REPLAN_PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE on every governed decision because the LLM Planner Pool is async while RuntimePlanner is sync. This change bridges the two through a NEW durable entity `replan_generation` (contract pair-replan-generation.v1): the sync bridge (ServePlannerDeps.replanProvider, PAIR_ASYNC_REPLAN_PROVIDER=1, default OFF) mints/inspects a deterministic per-(recovery_id, attempt_index) row binding mission, recovery decision, superseded plan, failure-context snapshot and slot index, then throws REPLAN_GENERATION_PENDING (distinct non-FAIL_CLOSED wait code) — runReplan treats it as NOT a failure: no candidate slot, no ledger row, runtime stays REPLANNING. An async driver (ReplanGenerationService claim/settle/reconcile + makeReplanGenerationDriver sweep on the existing 1s supervisor interval) claims PENDING rows under a bounded durable CAS lease+deadline (single-flight, restart-safe re-claim, bounded claim count), invokes the SAME runPlannerFailover composition (invokePlannerPool extracted verbatim from planExpander — eligibility re-proof, canonicalize+validatePlanProposal winner-check, planner_run/attempt evidence, run deadline) under canonical Objective lineage cost admission, and settles STAGED or FAILED with typed outcome. Staged candidates re-enter runReplan's committed gates (validatePlanProposal, bindPlanExternalInputs, assertPlanDataflow, semantic dedup, PREPARED→atomic commit) unchanged; canonical:true forwards pool-canonicalized tasks verbatim. Generation failures map onto FAIL_CLOSED_REPLAN_PROVIDER_* keeping REPLAN-infeasible to fresh-decision semantics. replan_context propagates into BOTH transports (codex-cli gains the field to the canonical buildPlannerUserPrompt).
